title: Billie Eilish to Headline BST Hyde Park for First Time: ‘She Inspires Fans, Challenges Our Industry to Be Better’
summary: "Billie continues to show what's possible when artists lead from the front," AEG Presents U.K. exec Jim King said.
contentText:
Billie Eilish will headline BST’s Hyde Park festival in 2027, joining the London festival’s stacked slate for next summer.

Related

Harry Styles Hits Festivals & Billie Eilish is Back: The Biggest Talking Points From Glastonbury’s 2027 Lineup Reveal

Eilish will headline the iconic venue on July 3, 2027, her first time performing at the festival. The announcement comes just days after she was revealed as one of Glastonbury’s headline artists in 2027. She first topped the festival bill in 2022, becoming the youngest solo act to ever do so.

She now joins Bon Jovi , Muse and RAYE as performers on the BST Hyde Park lineup for 2027, with more due to be announced in the coming weeks. Support acts for Eilish’s performance have not yet been shared.

Tickets for the performance go on presale from 3 p.m. GMT on Friday (Nov. 20) from the festival’s website , with a general sale commencing on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 10 a.m. local.

Speaking on the booking, Jim King, chief executive of AEG Presents U.K. and European Festival said she’d long been sought after for the festival. “Every event has their ‘list’ of a handful of artists you dream of seeing on its stage, and for BST Hyde Park, Billie Eilish has been at the top of that list for years,” King said in a statement.

He added, “Whether it’s her commitment to community and sustainability or her incredible live performances, Billie continues to show what’s possible when artists lead from the front. She inspires fans, challenges our industry to be better and delivers one of the most remarkable live shows anywhere in the world.”

Eilish last performed in the U.K. on her tour supporting third studio album Hit Me Hard and Soft , including six nights at London’s 20,000 capacity O2 Arena. The tour wrapped in November 2025 in San Francisco.
